📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Depuis janvier 2026, Bilal Benkhedim (25 ans), l'ancien Vert, vainqueur de la Coupe Gambardella 2019, opère dans les rangs du Mouloudia Club d'Oran, club de la Ligue 1 algérienne. Après un début de saison en demi-teinte, il s'installe peu à peu dans son équipe. Après une première entrée en jeu le 30 octobre contre l'Olympique Akbou, il a été titularisé le 4 novembre contre MC Alger, et tout récemment, vendredi dernier, contre la JS Saoura. Lors de ce match remporté 3-1 par le Mouloudia Club d'Oran (désormais 3ème au classement), il a inscrit le 2ème but dans le temps additionnel de la 1ère mi-temps, d'un magnifique tir de l'angle de la surface dans un angle fermé.

Le but de Bilal Benkhedim, c'est ici.

La carrière de Bilal Benkhedim à l'ASSE :.

- 2016-2017 : U17 nationaux avec Jean-Philippe Primard : 20 matchs, 6 buts- 2017-2018 : U17 nationaux avec Razik Nedder : 18 matchs, 23 buts ; U19 nationaux avec Lilian Compan : 2 matchs, 1 but.- 2018-2019 : U19 nationaux avec Razik Nedder : 9 matchs, 7 buts, victoire en Coupe Gambardella ; N2 avec Laurent Batlles : 13 matchs, 3 buts.- 2019-2020 : N2 avec Razik Nedder : 11 matchs, 2 buts ; pro avec Claude Puel : 3 matchs en L1, 1 match en Europa League, 1 match en Coupe de la Ligue, 1 match en Coupe de France.- 2020-2021 : N3 avec Razik Nedder : 1 match, 1 but ; pro avec Claude Puel : L1 : 3 matchs- 2021-2022 : N3 avec Razik Nedder : 8 matchs, 1 but.

Au niveau professionnel Bilal Benkhedim compte donc 6 matchs en L1, 1 match en Europa League, 1 en Coupe de la Ligue et 1 en Coupe de France.

#96011. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

📅 04 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5271 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that there was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago.
  • Sources indicate that everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025.
  • If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Sources indicate that everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a massive night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

According to recent reports, “With Alex, it is clear,” mentioned Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”.

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

Sources indicate that A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA.

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his fresh territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

It has been revealed that quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Sources indicate that iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move declared the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Recent findings suggest that your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

It has been revealed that inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm.

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

Sources indicate that there will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

It has been revealed that “I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”.

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS.

Sources indicate that “He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”.

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw.

Sources indicate that “We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”.

Cody Gakpo was linked with both Tottenham and Manchester City during the transfer window but stayed at Liverpool and has been in good form in these first three games of the season. He has assisted all three of Alexander Isak’s goals so far.

“You have to believe in yourself and have the belief of the fans that you are the man when you come for that much money. He had a terrible injury last year, but you can hear the Liverpool fans. They absolutely love what they saw. Some of his skills, his movement. That comes from his goal last week and the confidence that brings. Fingers crossed he can carry this on.”.

The final whistle goes at Portman Road and Andoni Iraola picks up his first win as Liverpool boss with a 2-0 victory thanks to Isak’s quickfire double inside the opening 10 minutes. Like they did two seasons ago, Liverpool win 2-0 at Portman Road.

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they at the moment protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Industry observers note that szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

In a recent development, tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Recent findings suggest that mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

It has been revealed that A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an crucial clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

According to recent reports, lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

According to recent reports, szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Sources indicate that emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

In a recent development, another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

In a recent development, inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm.

According to recent reports, liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

Sources indicate that A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA.

Recent findings suggest that wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

We are under way at Portman Road.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Portman Road and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

The Paraguayan is in his second stint at Ipswich and has two assists to his name in the first two league games.

Recent findings suggest that "He is the talisman already inside these first two games"Can Julio Enciso provide another assist tonight? 👀 pic.twitter.com/FaDkndt3BG.

According to recent reports, “It gives us a big belief that we can compete at the level. Coming up from the Championship, there is always some doubt around. The home win over Sunderland was huge for us. And then to be in the game for as long as we were at Manchester United was impressive. I have challenged the lads a lot. We do not focus on the outcome or results, we just commit to being the best version of ourselves. We cannot go toe-to-toe with everyone. We have to be sensible and smart.”.

Andoni Iraola has made a change at right-back tonight, with Ronaldu Araujo replacing Jeremie Frimpong. Araujo arrived at Liverpool this summer on loan with an option to buy from Barcelona.

A first Reds start for Ronald 💪 pic.twitter.com/P80pwhlBJ9.

"He's ready, definitely we will use him in the second half" Andoni Iraola says Bradley Barcola has looked good in training and is hoping to give him some game time against Ipswich ⏳ pic.twitter.com/C00WVI7ACd.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

Recent findings suggest that “We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola mentioned. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

Industry observers note that “He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”.

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

In a recent development, “What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil remarked. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”.

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

Dopo le rassicurazioni a Gattuso, il club valuta un ritocco dell’ingaggio: prima affronterà i contratti in scadenza nel 2028.

Recent findings suggest that kenneth Taylor vuole restare alla Lazio a gennaio e il club pensa a un ritocco del suo ingaggio. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, il centrocampista ha rassicurato Gattuso dopo l’interesse arrivato dalla Premier League e dalla Juventus. La società intende occuparsi prima dei contratti in scadenza nel 2028, poi affrontare anche la sua situazione.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that durante la sosta della scorsa settimana a Formello, Rino era in allarme per le sirene del mercato. Sono bastate poche parole di Taylor per tranquillizzarlo. Il giocatore gli ha confermato l’interesse ricevuto: «È tutto vero, i miei agenti mi hanno informato.» Gli ha però chiarito che non intende partire a gennaio: «Ma ho già detto che a gennaio non ci penso proprio ad andare via.».

Recent findings suggest that taylor ha espresso a Gattuso anche il suo obiettivo: «Voglio restare qui e aiutare la Lazio a tornare in Champions». Il tecnico non si aspettava questa risposta e ne è stato molto felice. Isaksen e Provstgaard gli avevano già promesso fedeltà e appartenenza. A 24 anni, Taylor è descritto come un giocatore già affermato, pronto per un salto di livello e capace di trovare posto in molte grandi squadre italiane e non solo.

Anche Fabiani e Lotito vogliono trattenere Taylor. Se il suo percorso proseguirà così, a giugno potrebbero non bastare neppure 40 milioni di euro per convincerli a trattare con Juventus, Brentford e Bournemouth. La Lazio vuole ricompensarlo per l’attaccamento mostrato e per aver rinunciato a guadagni più alti offerti altrove.

In a recent development, dopo aver affrontato i contratti in scadenza nel 2028, il club parlerà di un possibile adeguamento per Kenneth, che percepisce 1,7 milioni di euro fino al 2030. A febbraio riceverà il secondo premio fedeltà da 190mila euro, dopo aver scelto per la seconda volta di restare in biancoceleste. Acquistato dall’Ajax per meno di 17 milioni di euro, con il club olandese che conserva il 10% su una futura rivendita, Taylor si è rivelato un colpo straordinario per la Lazio.

Alors qu'il vit sa 4e saison (sur les 5 dernières) en Ligue 2, le supporter stéphanois a développé une théorie selon laquelle tous les adversaires jouent le match de leur vie à Geoffroy Guichard.

Ce soir le Nantes de Grégory Poirier (avec Cafaro mais sans Sow, blessé au genou) - autre club historique plongé dans l'enfer de cette division - a l’occasion de revenir à 16pts des Verts, en cas de victoire à domicile contre le Grenoble d’Yvann Maçon (et de Jules Mouton non convoqué).

Interrogé en conférence de presse sur les difficultés des Canaris à s’imposer à la Beaujoire (1 victoire en 6 matchs), le coach nantais a également fait sienne cette fameuse théorie :.

Recent findings suggest that « On le voit souvent, beaucoup d’équipes font leur meilleur match à l’extérieur à Nantes ou à Saint-Etienne parce que c’est un rendez-vous qu’ils ont coché, et ça il faut l’accepter on doit jouer avec ça. ».

Heureusement à Sainté, les hommes de Cathro l’ont manifestement mieux accepté avec 6 victoires en 6 matchs à GG.

According to recent reports, promu en Ligue 1 en mai dernier au nez et à la barbe d'un club formateur qui ne lui aura guère fait confiance (8 minutes temps additionnel compris en équipe première contre le QSG dans le Chaudron le 28 novembre 2021), Lucas Calodat (24 ans) a vu sa valeur multipliée par 30 depuis qu'il a quitté Sainté l'été 2023. Il est en effet estimé par Transfermarkt à 3 M€, soit 1,2 M€ de plus que le joueur qui occupe actuellement son poste chez les Verts (Ben Old, de la même génération 2002).

Meilleur joueur sarthois de la saison en cours et 34e meilleur joueur de l'élite selon Sofascore (ex aequo avec le capitaine du Paris FC Pierre Lees-Melou et celui des vilains Corentin Tolisso), le dynamique piston gauche manceau a brillé hier sous un maillot vert et blanc au Vélodrome où il s'est imposé en clôture de la 11e journée de L1 sous le regard aussi médusé que consterné de Théo Vermot et Neal Maupay (restés sur le banc phocéen) car l'OM menait encore 2-0 à la 70e minute...

La Pravda lui donne la meilleure note de cette rencontre (7/10), assortie du commentaire suivant : "Oui, le travail défensif est parfois un peu aléatoire, il a oublié Amine Harit (7e) et n'est peut-être pas net au départ de l'action qui a amené le second but de l'OM. Mais quelle débauche d'énergie et quel pied gauche ! Capable d'éliminer Harit avec aisance (17e). Un centre bien travaillé vers la tête de Gueye, non cadrée (28e). Une bonne incursion et un bon ballon pour Gueye (45e+1). Un centre mal exploité (64e), mais c'est lui, du pied droit, qui a trouvé Colas pour l'égalisation (2-2, 84e).".

In a recent development, ouest-France considère que le natif de Paris a été le meilleur à Marseille. Le quotidien régional le plus diffusé de France lui décerne en effet un joli 8/10. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

PSV returned to the top of the Eredivisie with a thumping 5-2 win over Cambuur Leeuwarden as previous leaders Feyenoord lost a seven-goal thriller against the other Frisian club, Heerenveen.

It took just 46 seconds for PSV to get off the mark as Sven Mijnans headed in unmarked.

The midfielder added a second after 15 minutes and completed his hat-trick with a free-kick in the 80th minute to make the score 4-2, just as Cambuur were threatening a comeback.

Feyenoord’s dip in form continued as they let a two-goal lead slip at Heerenveen. The Rotterdammers looked to be in control going into the break with a trademark drilled shot by Anis Hadj Moussa and a penalty by Nacho Ferri.

But Maas Willemsen bundled in the ball from a corner on the stroke of half-time, before Ringo Meerveld came on for the second half and scored a hat-trick as Feyenoord’s defence crumbled under pressure.

“In the matches when we played well I saw a team that fought for each other,” Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst stated after the game. “Mentally strong, kept running even when we didn’t have the ball. That’s our strength. When we don’t do that we’re a lesser team.”.

Mexx Meerdink scored a hotly contested late penalty to settle a tempestuous game in Alkmaar as AZ came back from 3-1 down against Groningen to claim their first win in five matches.

In a recent development, goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen was given a second yellow card for protesting too hard against the decision to penalise him for upending Ayoub Oufkir. Once the commotion died down Meerdink, who had missed from the spot against Vaessen earlier in the second half, made no mistake against substitute goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar.

Ajax missed the chance to take over top spot at Twente as their former striker Wout Weghorst scored a last-minute penalty to rescue a point for the home side.

Ajax had been 2-0 up with a bullet header by their giant striker Tolu Arokodare and a long-range strike by Rayane Bounida, before an own goal by Dies Janse brought the visitors back into the game.

Fortuna Sittard also had to settle for a point against Telstar after going 2-0 up thanks to a bizarre own goal by Sem Valk. The defender’s sliced clearance looped over the head of Ronald Koeman Junior as the goalkeeper tried to head it away rather than risk being penalised for handling a backpass.

Goals just before half-time by Abdelnour Soualhia and Patrick Brouwer brought Telstar back into the game, but neither side was able to find a winner after the break.

That result allowed ADO, under the guidance of interim coach Levi Schwiebbe, to close the gap on 16th-placed Telstar to one point with a 3-1 win against Sparta, while bottom Willem II collected their third point of the season at home to PEC Zwolle.

ADO Den Haag 3-1 Sparta Rotterdam.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 2-5 PSV Eindhoven.

#95997. Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

📅 05 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3256 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3256 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources.
  • It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.
  • “Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

“Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

“I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”.

What a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

According to recent reports, another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

To say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

According to recent reports, the warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

It has been revealed that the Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton noted after dodging that bullet.

Industry observers note that and although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

It could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

It promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”.

Could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

Sources indicate that “Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”.

Sources indicate that gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My plan is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

According to recent reports, he seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

Sources indicate that he told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”.

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”.

According to recent reports, alpine managing director Steve Nielsen said to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

“We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”.

Here’s what he remarked immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”.

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY.

He notes: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”.

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who remarked he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

Alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

Recent findings suggest that his tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

In a recent development, piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

He starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Piastri may be in for some bother.

Sources indicate that hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql.

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs.

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

According to recent reports, alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu.

Industry observers note that pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

Monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a substantial opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2.

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car firm makes sense, despite what I noted earlier.

It has been revealed that sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC.

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

Industry observers note that the Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”.

Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M.

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6.

I’m as massive a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car organization, isn’t there?

Sources indicate that 🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx.

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI.

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

Sources indicate that “Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’.

“Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

In a recent development, “What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”.

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

It has been revealed that schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft.

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

Industry observers note that A near miss for Oscar Piastri! 😬 pic.twitter.com/y6UMu8wIDM.

The pair are just natural friends.

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT.

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton noted yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”.

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

The full list of times from earlier today.

FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he remarked.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”.

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

Recent findings suggest that however, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

Vous l'attendiez, le voici, le voilà, le désormais fameux tour d'horizon des Verts partis s'exiler pour plus (et mieux) jouer.

Sources indicate that tandis que leurs anciens coéquipiers ont frappé un grand coup en ramenant les 3pts de Reims, les joueurs prêtés par l’ASSE ont joué plus que d’ordinaire ce week-end, à défaut de briller particulièrement. Bonne nouvelle en effet, ils étaient 5 sur 9 alignés d’entrée en attendant le match du Rapid Bucarest ce soir.

Du côté des championnats étrangers, Igor Miladinovic confirme son statut de pilier au Partizan Belgrade. Il a ainsi vécu sa 12e titularisation en championnat ce week-end pour une nouvelle défaite sur la pelouse de l’MT Belgrade (1-2) dans un des nombreux derbies de la capitale serbe. Il totalise désormais 969 minutes de jeu (plus 113 en Coupe d’Europe) et le Partizan Belgrade reste 10e sur 14 après 16 journées.

Son voisin Strahinja Stojkovic a connu une troisième titularisation de suite (la 5e cette saison), pour une troisième défaite (0-2) avec l’OFK Belgrade désormais avant dernier du championnat. Stojkovic est donc relégable et compte désormais 386 minutes de jeu.

En Roumanie, avant le match du Rapid Bucarest ce soir, le temps de jeu de Annan restait réduit : 241 minutes en championnat, et une dernière titularisation (la 3e) qui remonte au 18 septembre.

It has been revealed that direction l’Espagne ou Lucas Stassin réalise un début de saison mitigé. Il était certes de nouveau titulaire avec le FC Séville dans le derby face au Betis et s’est montré actif, mais il n’a pas eu l’occasion de briller et est sorti à la vilaine 69e minute, avant que son équipe égalise (1-1). Il compte désormais 541 minutes de jeu en Liga en 8 matchs (6 titularisations et 2 sorties de banc) et a marqué 1 but et délivré 1 passe décisive.

En d2 espagnole, les choses se compliquent pour Aïmen Moueffek. Son équipe réagit … mais sans lui. Pour la 2e fois de suite, il est resté scotché sur le banc, et Cadix l’a emporté 3-0 sur la pelouse de l’équipe B de la Real Sociedad. Son bilan reste de 202 minutes de jeu en championnat (3 titularisations) et 45 en coupe, alors qu’ont déjà été jouées 15 journées de championnat.

Dans l’Hexagone, l’éclaircie bourguignonne se confirme : En effet, si Djylian N’Guessan a de nouveau vu son équipe s’imposer depuis le banc de touche et continue d’afficher un très maigre temps de jeu avec Brest (28 minutes de jeu depuis le début de saison), Pierre Ekwah a connu sa seconde titularisation de suite, avec un nul (1-1) décroché par Auxerre à Monaco. Il totalise désormais 223 minutes de jeu.

Sources indicate that A Pau toujours rien de neuf pour Luan Gadegbeku (photo) qui, après sa titularisation en Coupe, est retourné sur le banc ce week-end. Il reste sur son maigre total de 147 minutes de jeu (plus 90 en Coupe). En revanche Axel Dodote a connu une 7e titularisation sur la pelouse du Red Star avec Pau, la première depuis début septembre, profitant notamment de l’absence de Briançon en défense centrale. Hélas il est sorti à la 53e . Son temps de jeu est désormais de 526 minutes.

The most famous name in Dutch football could appear on an international men’s team sheet for the first time in 30 years after Johan Cruyff’s grandson was called up for the United States’ upcoming matches in Europe.

Shae Cruijff-Beane, the son of Johan Cruyff’s daughter Chantal and her American husband Todd Beane, was included in the squad that will play against Norway and Portugal in the next seven days.

Cruijff-Beane plays as a midfielder for Gimnàstic de Tarragona, a club in the Spanish third tier based near Barcelona. His older brother Jordan also came through the club’s ranks and is currently playing US college football at Westmont College in California.

Shae, 17, is eligible to play for the USA through his father and Spain and the Netherlands through his mother, who spent part of her childhood in Catalonia while Johan Cruyff was playing for Barcelona in the 1970s.

The USA under-18 squad also includes an Ajax player, midfielder Xander Newstead, who grew up in San Francisco and joined the Amsterdam club’s youth team set-up at the age of 10, beforec signing professional terms last year.

Johan Cruyff went on to play in the United States for Los Angeles Aztecs and Washington Diplomats before returning to the Netherlands, winding down his career at Ajax and Feyenoord.

In a recent development, his son Jordi played for Barcelona and Manchester United and won nine international caps in 1996. Last year he was appointed technical director at Ajax, the club where his father began his career.

Breaking: Ces Lorrains ne sont pas des quiches

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Après 13 journées, l’ASNL a déjà empoché plus de points (28) que sur l’ensemble du championnat de L2 de la saison 2021-2022 ponctuée par sa relégation en National (27 points) !
  • Recent findings suggest that oswald Tanchot commente la magnifique dynamique de son équipe dans L’Est Républicain.

Après 13 journées, l’ASNL a déjà empoché plus de points (28) que sur l’ensemble du championnat de L2 de la saison 2021-2022 ponctuée par sa relégation en National (27 points) ! Restant sur une impressionnante série de 7 victoires avant de défier les leaders stéphanois le 5 décembre dans le Chaudron pour le match au sommet de la 14e journée, les surprenants dauphins nancéiens viennent d’égaler la plus grande série de succès de l’histoire du club au chardon. Cela faisait 52 ans que Nancy n’avait pas réussi une telle performance. Lors de cet exercice 1974-1975, un certain Michel Platini (19 ans à l’époque) avait réussi sa première saison pleine en claquant 17 pions en 32 matches de D2. Il s’était aussi illustré cette saison-là en marquant pas moins de 13 buts en Coupe de France dont 3 en 8e de finale contre son futur club stéphanois, qui filait alors vers son dernier doublé de l’histoire.

Recent findings suggest that oswald Tanchot commente la magnifique dynamique de son équipe dans L’Est Républicain. "Notre force, c’est d’avoir un vestiaire aussi sain. On a des joueurs qui sont dans une logique de collectif en permanence, ça se voit sur le terrain et ça nous aide à aller chercher les victoires. Les joueurs qui entrent dans l’équipe, que ce soit au coup d’envoi ou en cours de match, apportent souvent quelque chose. Il faut absolument garder cet état d’esprit. Il y a beaucoup de solidarité dans notre jeu, des fermetures de passes pour l’adversaire parce que tous nos joueurs font les efforts dans le replacement. Ces petits détails font une grande différence. On voulait se donner le droit d’avoir une affiche magnifique à Geoffroy-Guichard. Mais avant de penser à Saint-Etienne, on souhaite négocier au mieux ce 8e tour de Coupe de France contre Furiani (National 1).".

L'ancien Vert, Vagner Dias Goncalves (32 ans) joue désormais, depuis le 1er septembre, en deuxième division chypriote, dans le club du FC Ethnikos Achnas. C'était, ce week-end la 8ème journée du championnat, et les  coéquipiers de Vagner l'ont largement emporté (7-0) sur ASIL Lysi. Titulaire pour la 1ère fois de la saison, l'ancien Vert a inscrit un doublé aux 2ème et 31ème minutes. Le FC Ethnikos Achnas est leader avec 7 victoires et 1 défaite.

Les images du match, c'est ici.

Le Capverdien Vagner Dias Goncalves était arrivé à l'ASSE en 2017. La saison 2017-2018, il avait participé à 4 matchs de L1 (106 minutes de jeu), et un match de Coupe de France. Le plus souvent en équipe N3 de Laurent Batlles, il avait accédé à la N2 et inscrit 6 buts.La saison suivante, 2018-2019, il n'a fait aucune apparition en pro, jouant donc en N2, toujours sous les ordres de Laurent Batlles. Il y inscrit 6 buts mais ne convainc pas au point d'être prêté à l'AS Nancy (en 2 saisons, il joue 33 matchs et inscrit 13 buts) puis transféré au FC Metz en 2020. Le club lorrain le prêtera au FC Sion (2021-2022) puis au RFC Seraing, en Belgique, (2022-2023) où il avait retrouvé Aurélien Remoué et Marvin Tshibuabua.

En janvier 2024, il a signé dans le club polonais de de Radomiak Radom, puis en mai 2025 dans le club brésilien d'Amazonas pour une pige de 4 mois. Sans club pendant un an, il a rejoint, le mois dernier, le championnat de Chypre.

La Lazio di Gattuso ha raccolto nelle prime dodici giornate più punti di quella del 2000, considerata tra le più forti della storia biancoceleste per l’organico al completo. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Da quando la vittoria vale tre punti, soltanto la Juventus, prima con Capello e poi con Allegri, ha fatto meglio. È da questi numeri che Il Messaggero parte per accostare le due squadre, pur tenendo distinte le rispettive epoche.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Rino, Frattesi e gli altri biancocelesti continuano a guardare al traguardo dei 40 punti, indicato come quota della salvezza matematica. Dopo la vittoria sul Lecce, il tecnico calabrese aveva spiegato: «E dopo parleremo di altro, con maggiore tranquillità».

According to recent reports, il confronto con la squadra del secondo scudetto riguarda anche lo spogliatoio. Gattuso vi ha portato un clima che richiama, con le dovute proporzioni, quello creato da Eriksson ventisei anni fa. Nella Lazio di allora, però, l’armonia non era quella di oggi: convivevano il gruppo degli ex Samp, guidato da Roberto Mancini, e quello degli argentini, senza un capo designato ma rappresentato dalle personalità di Veron e Simeone.

In a recent development, il paragone suggerito dalla partita contro il Lecce è quello tra Belahyane e Almeyda. Il marocchino intercetta palloni e li sottrae agli avversari commettendo raramente fallo, come faceva l’argentino. Almeyda era chiamato Capitan Uncino per il modo in cui usava il piede destro per portare via il pallone; Belahyane si affida invece alla rapidità della corsa e all’appoggio del corpo sul rivale per interrompere l’azione.

Tra i portieri, Mandas richiama Luca Marchegiani: entrambi efficaci tra i pali, dotati di personalità sulle palle alte e meno talentuosi nel gioco con i piedi. A Marchegiani costò il posto in Nazionale un errore che Sacchi non gli perdonò.

A centrocampo, Frattesi ricorda Nedved quando arriva nei pressi dell’area pronto a colpire. Il ceco era un attaccante aggiunto per Zoff ed Eriksson; Davide è l’incursore della squadra di Gattuso. Alcuni movimenti di Taylor richiamano Stankovic, più potente soprattutto nel tiro dalla distanza. L’olandese viene accostato anche a Simeone per la capacità di contribuire con gol e assist senza dare nell’occhio.

Morgan Guilavogui (28 ans), le jeune frère de Josuha évolue en MLS (Conférence ouest), au Real Salt Lake, depuis le 3 février 2026, après avoir porté les couleurs de l'ASSE (formation), du SC Toulon, du Paris FC, du RC Lens et du FC St Pauli.

Vendredi, à l'heure de jeu, contre les Seattle Sounders, dans les playoffs de la MLS Cup, il a inscrit le but égalisateur d'un superbe tir de la demi-lune, tir qui s'est logé dans la lucarne adverse . C'était le 5ème but de la saison pour Morgan Guilavogui. (1 en Leagues Cup, 5 en MLS League soccre, et 1 en MLS Cup Playoffs).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

According to recent reports, newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Sources indicate that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Recent findings suggest that ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

It has been revealed that “It indicates where we have potential,” he stated. “There are elements to improve offensively.

In a recent development, “The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed major character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”.

According to recent reports, A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

Sources indicate that in truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a fresh manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It has been revealed that it is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

According to recent reports, that opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

According to recent reports, bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

It has been revealed that tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj.

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Industry observers note that justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Sources indicate that bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”.

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx.

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9.

Industry observers note that dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

In a recent development, smith clatters into Barnes for a late booking. It’s wave after wave of Newcastle pressure at the moment as Barnes wins a free-kick against Cook.

The noise inside St James’ Park is incredible. The home fans are roaring on the Newcastle players to find a third goal. Bournemouth look absolutely exhausted.

Sources indicate that amid the late drama, Bournemouth make another two changes as Gannon-Doak and Jebbison replace Tavernier and Rayan. There will be six minutes of added time. Can either side find a late winner?

Bournemouth fail to deal with a looped cross into their penalty area and can’t clear the danger. Barnes’ initial effort is blocked and the ball breaks to Ramsey, who slams a clinical low strike into the bottom corner to send the Newcastle fans wild. The hosts from come from two goals down, but can they go on and win it now?

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

Murphy does brilliantly to beat Truffert to the ball and drive down the wing. The Bournemouth defender has a hold of his shirt and is booked.

Scott rolls a short free-kick into Tavernier, who is allowed to carry the ball to the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. After a few touches, he shoots, but his thunderous effort comfortably flies off target.

The current state of the game suits Bournemouth. There’s been a lot of fouls from both sides, halting the rhythm. It’s been very stop-start in this second half.

In a recent development, safe to say that the Newcastle fans are not happy with the referee. Fernandez-Pardo stands on Smith, giving Bournemouth a free-kick. The home support loudly boo the decision.

According to recent reports, newcastle respond with another double substitution. Steur and Murphy are on, with Nico and Elanga departing the action.

Fernandez-Pardo has been tasked with unlocking Bournemouth’s defence in this closely-fought encounter, but is still waiting for his moment.

Kluivert hauls new signing Fernandez-Pardo and is given a yellow card, prompting cheers from the Newcastle fans.

Industry observers note that it looks like Fernandez-Pardo will slot into the No.10 position behind Wissa as Newcastle continue their search for an equaliser. Bournemouth are defending well as a unit in this second half.

According to recent reports, newcastle’s double-change is here as Fernandez-Pardo comes on for his debut, replacing Willock. The other alteration sees Ramsey come on for Miley.

Newcastle have been the more aggressive side since the restart. Hall cuts inside and after receiving a short corner and shoots, but his effort is high and wide. Fernandez-Pardo and Ramsey look like they’re stepping up their respective warm-ups as they prepare to enter the action.

Wissa is booked for unceremoniously barging Adams in an off-the-ball collision. Jaissle can’t believe it and passionately demonstrates his frustration towards the referee and fourth official.

Just like the first half, there’s also been a fast start to the second. Both managers are still pacing up and down their technical areas.

Newcastle are so close to a leveller! Wissa drives forward from inside Newcastle’s half, then dribbles away from Scott, before skipping past Silva. He manufactures some space and clips a pinpoint cross into Willock, who glances a header agonisingly wide of the far post. That was brilliant play from Wissa.

Newcastle get in behind Bournemouth’s backline as Willock latches onto Hall’s through ball. The former Arsenal academy graduate plays in Barnes, whose one-on-one attempt is smothered by Petrovic. The offside flag was then raised against the Newcastle attacker.

We are back under way for the second half. Here we go again.

It has been revealed that it’s end-to-end at St James’ Park. This game is being played like a basketball match. Both teams are flying forward in numbers at every opportunity.

Oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

There was misfortune after with the ball spinning into his own net off Malick Thiaw but Newcastle have been abject.

Easily the worst half an hour of Matthias Jaissle’s short time in charge and as bad as anything we have seen from Newcastle in front of their own supporters for a while.

Despite having a miserable record against Bournemouth in recent years, Newcastle will be expected to win this afternoon. The atmosphere, electric for the opener against Liverpool and the return of villain Alexander Isak, will be more expectant today.

These are the fixtures Eddie Howe’s team repeatedly slipped up in at home last season, where the likes of Everton, Brentford, Bournemouth and Sunderland all won.

Can Jaissle improve that record? Can his team thrive when they are likely to have more of the ball, play against a low block defence and an opponent adept at lightning-fast counterattacks?

Does the German’s “vertical” football have as much success against a team that does not play a high defensive line as Liverpool and Tottenham did?

We are likely to know a lot more about Newcastle after this game. There has been a lot of hype and excitement after an impressive start to the newly introduced season but have people got a little carried away?

Let’s see how they get on against a Bournemouth side that probably should have got at least a point away to Manchester City in their opening away game.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets in the spring, Matías Fernandez-Pardo featured prominently.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under upcoming head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

It has been revealed that despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

Dutch progress in Nations League despite 5-0 drubbing in Germany

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (381 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dutchnews

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

The Netherlands came crashing down to earth after hammering Greece as they were outclassed and outmuscled by Germany in Berlin.

Oranje went into the final match of the Nations League group stage with high hopes of recording their first win over their old rivals in seven matches stretching back to 2019.

Instead they suffered their second worst defeat ever at the hands of Germany, but still progressed to the knockout stages thanks to their thumping 7-0 win in Amsterdam on Friday.

Coach Xavi Hernandez was forced to make one change in midfield as Jurriën Timber replaced Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong, who pulled out with an obturator muscle strain.

Germany shaded the first half and went ahead five minutes before the break when Freiburg striker Derry Scherhant cut in from the left hand side and beat Bart Verbruggen with a curling strike into the top corner.

Scherhant had struck the post minutes earlier, while the Dutch might have taken the lead earlier when Crysencio Summerville slipped in the penalty area as he tried to control a cross by Cody Gakpo.

But in the second half the Dutch fell apart. In the 60th minute Florian Wirtz shoved Denzel Dumfries off the ball and had space to tee up a left-footed shot from the edge of the area that gave Verbruggen no chance.

Nico Schlotterbeck added a third from a free-kick five minutes later, before Wirtz drifted past Gakpo on the right side of the penalty area to score his second.

The humiliation was complete when Brajan Gruda capped a fine attacking performance by firing in a rebound.

In a recent development, dumfries made no excuses afterwards for what he admitted was a “terrible performance”. “We gave the ball away too easily, left too much space and were too weak in the challenges,” he told NOS. “We can’t let that happen.”.

As part of PortuGOAL’s efforts to constantly evolve and serve lovers of Portuguese football with top-quality and increasingly accessible content, we are replacing the PortuGOAL Android and Apple APPs with a new Progressive Web Application (PWA) as from tomorrow, Tuesday 3 April.

Sources indicate that this big step forward in phone apps technology loads the content instantly, even in areas of low connectivity, stays up to date at all times, displays the most recent version upon launching, is more efficient than native apps, works on-demand and is always accessible, without taking up a smartphone’s valuable memory or data.
